summary: 70 exact definitions of ICT-style 1-minute structures x 6 horizons = 420 looks on six Binance perpetuals, 2020-2023. 181 looks have day-clustered |t| > 3, but 110 of them point against the textbook reading, and no effect up to 15 minutes exceeds 5.1 bp gross versus 12-14 bp taker costs. Break of structure, fair value gaps, order blocks, compression breakouts, displacement and previous-day sweeps give nothing tradeable; limit orders at gap or block edges lose 0.9-1.3 bp to adverse selection (t -17, -32). The only cost-sized effect is the rebound after a sweep of the 4-hour extreme: +19.4 bp at 240 min on design (t 4.0, net of taker costs +6.0) and +18.8 bp on validation (t 3.5, net +5.3, t of net 1.0). It is not specific to the pattern, sits on the long side and in altcoins, and faded to about zero in 2023. Resting orders net +14.1 / +14.1 bp per fill at maker fees (t 2.8 / 2.6). Part B: waiting for a structure did not improve trend-trade fills: small sweep +10.3 bp (t 1.8) design, +3.0 (t 0.5) validation; waiting for a break of structure made 66%-75% of fills worse (-9.4 bp, t -2.3, validation).

entry_timing: Daily trend rule = blend of 50/100/200-day SMA filters on BTC and ETH spot; every weight change is filled at 00:00 UTC. Improvement = price at the 00:00 open versus price after waiting for the first structure in the trade's direction (spot 1-minute bars; positive = better). ENTRIES, wait up to 4 h -- small sweep (N30, 2 bp, k3): design 147 trades: mean +2.6 bp, median +14.4, t 0.34, worse in 26%; validation 63 trades: mean +8.4 bp, median +12.7, t 2.04, worse in 24%. Big sweep (N240, 10 bp, k1), up to 4 h (occurs in 23% / 6% of cases, otherwise bought 4 h later): design 147 trades: mean +15.8 bp, median +35.0, t 1.31, worse in 30%; validation 63 trades: mean +7.7 bp, median +16.6, t 0.73, worse in 38%; up to 24 h: design 147 trades: mean +12.7 bp, median +66.4, t 0.71, worse in 34%; validation 63 trades: mean -15.4 bp, median +7.0, t -0.59, worse in 46%. Companion triggers (not selected in Part A): bullish break of structure: design 147 trades: mean -1.5 bp, median -11.0, t -0.27, worse in 69%; validation 63 trades: mean -9.5 bp, median -9.4, t -2.84, worse in 78%; return into a bullish fair value gap: design 147 trades: mean +0.9 bp, median +2.5, t 0.18, worse in 48%; validation 63 trades: mean -1.2 bp, median +1.9, t -0.26, worse in 44%. EXITS (mirror), small sweep: design 137 trades: mean +18.6 bp, median +17.7, t 2.22, worse in 25%; validation 69 trades: mean -1.9 bp, median +13.6, t -0.18, worse in 26%; big sweep up to 24 h: design 136 trades: mean +15.7 bp, median +67.2, t 0.44, worse in 34%; validation 69 trades: mean -88.5 bp, median -16.0, t -2.26, worse in 55%; break of structure: design 137 trades: mean +3.2 bp, median -10.4, t 0.56, worse in 63%; validation 69 trades: mean -9.3 bp, median -9.0, t -1.31, worse in 72%. ENTRIES AND EXITS TOGETHER, small sweep: design 284 trades: mean +10.3 bp, median +15.5, t 1.82, worse in 25%; validation 132 trades: mean +3.0 bp, median +13.0, t 0.53, worse in 25%; break of structure: design 284 trades: mean +0.8 bp, median -10.5, t 0.19, worse in 66%; validation 132 trades: mean -9.4 bp, median -9.2, t -2.34, worse in 75%. Higher-powered supplement, every calendar day, both sides, small sweep: design 5744 trades: mean +4.2 bp, median +11.4, t 4.28, worse in 33%; validation 2188 trades: mean +1.3 bp, median +8.1, t 1.05, worse in 32%. Typical shape: the wait gives a better price about three times in four (by 20-40 bp) and a worse one the fourth time (by 60-80 bp), so the mean is statistically zero. Nothing is significant in both segments; the only consistent feature is that waiting for a break of structure (confirmation) gives a worse price in 63-78% of trades (its mean cost is significant on validation only). At 13-16x annual one-way turnover of the trend rule, each bp of fill improvement is worth 0.13-0.16% of equity per year.
caveats: Verdict 'edge_only_with_maker_fills' rests on ONE pre-registered pair (sweep of the 4-hour extreme, 240-minute hold). Its taker net (+6.0 design, +5.3 validation) is not distinguishable from zero (t 1.3 and 1.0); the maker figure assumes a passive exit at the open price 240 minutes later (optimistic); with a taker exit it is +9.4 / +9.4 bp (t 1.9 / 1.7).

The effect is not a property of the 'liquidity sweep' pattern: on design, a thrust to a new 4-hour low was followed by the same rebound whether the bar closed back inside (sweep) or price stayed below for three closes (acceptance). It is a generic dip-rebound, on the long side only; the short side (sweeps of highs) earns nothing.

It is unstable in time and across coins: about zero in 2023 (+2.7 bp at 240 min, t 0.2) and weak in the last 18 months of design (2022-07..2023-12: +8.8 bp, t 1.5), back in 2024-25; carried by XRP, SOL, DOGE, BNB. For BTC and ETH alone the validation figure is +4.0 bp (t 0.6) on perpetuals and about the same on spot.

This is an event study, not a portfolio backtest: events come in bursts across correlated coins (many per sell-off), so a small account could take only a fraction of them; capital limits, overlapping positions, funding payments and liquidation risk while buying falling prices are not modelled.

Fills are assumed at the next 1-minute open with 1-2 bp slippage. These events occur in the fastest minutes of the day, when spreads are widest, so taker results are more likely over- than under-stated. Bars cannot show queue position; the resting-order simulation counts a fill only when price trades strictly through the order.

Multiple testing: 420 looks on design (plus 420 on PAXG, reported separately, and year/coin/side splits of about 15 looks). Design figures of the selected pairs are biased upward by selection; the validation figures are not. Validation was evaluated once, for the three pre-registered pairs and the pre-registered diagnostics only. The hold-out (from 2025-07-01) was never loaded.

The long-only split of the selected pair (excess over baseline minus taker cost about +12-13 bp, t 2.1 design / 1.3 validation) was noticed on design before validation but was not pre-registered as its own test; treat it as a hypothesis for the hold-out, not a finding.

Part B has little power on the actual trend trades (284 design, 132 validation; standard errors of 4 to 25 bp depending on the structure). The all-days supplement narrows the unconditional effect of waiting for the small sweep to +4.2 bp (design) and +1.3 bp (validation). All Part B trades start at 00:00 UTC, an unusual minute (daily close, funding), so the result may not carry to other clock times.

The matched baseline uses volatility quintiles formed within each calendar year (a benchmark, not a signal, so it is not causal by construction). Disclosure: at the very start a data-availability printout of the full files (row counts, date range, number of gaps; no prices) was seen before the segments were separated in code.

PAXG (tokenised gold) cannot be judged on 1-minute bars: its tick is about 5 bp of price and about a third of its bars have no trade, so 379 of 420 looks are 'significant' through bid-ask bounce alone and none clears the 24 bp spot round trip.
question: Do structures detected on 1-minute bars predict returns by enough to pay costs (A), and does waiting for one improve the fill of a daily trend trade (B)?

selection.statement: Written after the design run and before any price, return or event dated 2024-01-01 or later was computed or looked at by this study. (Disclosure: a data-availability printout of the full files - row counts, first and last timestamps, number of gaps - was seen at the very start; it contains no prices.)

selected.why: Of the 420 looks, the only one with day-clustered |t| >= 3.9 (Bonferroni 5%) AND a positive mean after a taker round trip. Weakness known at selection time: the effect is on the long side (after sweeps of lows) and is concentrated in 2020-2021; 2023 is about zero.
The same structure at the horizon where the evidence is strongest (t = 6.2, positive in all four design years and all six coins). Gross about equals the taker cost, so it can only matter for a maker.

The most significant of all 420 looks (t = 12.2), same sign in every design year and every coin. Its size (about 1 bp) is an order of magnitude below any cost; it is carried forward to show whether the most robust statistical effect persists, not because it could be traded.

protocol.segment_rules: design = bars before 2024-01-01; validation = 2024-01-01 .. 2025-06-30; hold-out never loaded

part_a_validation.what: exactly the three (definition, horizon) pairs above, six perpetuals pooled, same code, same baseline construction, same clustering; spot BTC/ETH as cross-check; breakdown by year, coin and direction
part_a_validation.replicates_if: same sign as on design and day-clustered t of the excess over baseline >= 2.4 (two-sided 5% with a Bonferroni factor of 3)
part_a_validation.pays_taker_costs_if: mean gross minus the taker round trip > 0 with (gross - cost) / clustered s.e. >= 2, on design and on validation
part_a_validation.maker_diagnostic: maker_sim.py on the same three pairs: limit order at the event bar's close, resting 5 minutes, filled only on a strict trade-through; reported with a 4 bp (maker both sides) and a maker-in / taker-out cost. Counts as 'edge only with maker fills' if the 4 bp figure is > 0 with t >= 2 on design and on validation while the taker test fails.

part_b.rule: blend_weights() of research/baseline/trend_baseline.py on Binance spot daily closes of BTCUSDT and ETHUSDT; a change decided at the close of day D is executed at 00:00 UTC of day D+1
part_b.trades: every (coin, day) on which the target weight rises (entry: wait for the first BULLISH occurrence) or falls (exit: wait for the first BEARISH occurrence)
part_b.companion_note: not selected in Part A (no usable edge on design); included because 'wait for a 1-minute break of structure' and 'wait for the return into a fair value gap' are the entry triggers discretionary traders actually use. Reported separately from the selected ones.
part_b.fill: open of the minute after the first occurrence detected at or after the 00:00 bar; if none occurs, the open of the bar at 00:00 + window
part_b.measures: improvement in bp versus the 00:00 open (positive = better price), mean, median, day-clustered t, share of trades made worse, share triggered, mean wait; controls: waiting to the end of the window regardless, and the same waiting times applied without the structure (time-matched placebo)
part_b.markets: spot 1-minute bars (primary: the rule trades spot) and perpetual 1-minute bars (secondary)
part_b.supplement: the same comparison on EVERY calendar day (both sides), as a higher-powered check of whether waiting for the structure beats the open at all

synthetic_tests: 15 tests in test_eventstudy.py, all passing (out/test_log.txt): no look-ahead for all 70 definitions under altered and truncated futures; each detector equal to a literal loop implementation; forward-return alignment and gap handling; planted 2 bp/bar effect recovered; clustered t calibrated under bursts and overlap; baseline removes hour-of-day drift.
